extra.message: The endpoint returns internal exception details to the client, including str(exc) and exc.__class__.__name__ in the JSON response. The raised RuntimeError embeds the lot_ref input and the BASE_EXPORT_DIR server path, leaking sensitive implementation details and filesystem layout to callers (CWE-209).

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: The raw request body and the Authorization header value are written to the application log via logger.warning. Credentials/tokens supplied in the Authorization header and any sensitive data in the request body are persisted to logs (CWE-532).

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: The lane query parameter is passed directly to RedirectResponse(lane) with no validation or allow-list. An attacker can supply an absolute URL (e.g. https://evil.com) to redirect users to an arbitrary external site, enabling phishing (CWE-601).

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: pickle.loads(raw) deserializes attacker-controlled data (request body, query blob, or base64-decoded input). pickle is not safe for untrusted data and allows arbitrary code execution via crafted payloads, leading to remote code execution (CWE-502).

cwe: CWE-502: Deserialization of Untrusted Data

extra.message: workset.update(payload) blindly merges the entire user-supplied JSON payload into the workset dictionary. A caller can override security-sensitive defaults such as role, tier, approved, and balance, bypassing authorization/privilege assumptions (CWE-915).

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: The ref parameter (from query string or JSON body) is interpolated directly into BASE_EXPORT_DIR / f"{ref}.json" with no sanitization. A value containing path separators (e.g. ../../etc/foo) escapes the intended directory, allowing arbitrary file write (CWE-22).

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: The endpoint writes Social Security Numbers and payment card numbers (ssn/card fields, with real-looking defaults) to a JSON file on disk in plaintext via target.write_text(json.dumps(...)). Sensitive PII/payment data is stored unencrypted (CWE-312/CWE-359).

cwe: CWE-312: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information
CWE-359: Exposure of Private Personal Information

extra.message: hashlib.md5 is used to produce a digest of user-supplied input. MD5 is cryptographically broken and unsuitable for security-sensitive digests; a security-relevant hash should use SHA-256 or stronger (CWE-327).

cwe: CWE-327: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm

extra.message: The count query parameter is used directly as the upper bound of range(count) to build an in-memory list of rows with no limit. A caller can request an extremely large count, exhausting server memory/CPU and causing denial of service (CWE-400).

cwe: CWE-400: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption

extra.message: The endpoint query parameter is passed directly to urllib.request.urlopen(endpoint, ...). A caller can make the server fetch arbitrary URLs, including internal/cloud-metadata addresses (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/), enabling server-side request forgery (CWE-918).

cwe: CWE-918: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)

extra.message: Verifier secrets are hard-coded in source: known = {"north": "4812", "south": "5930"}. These shared credentials cannot be rotated without a code change and are visible to anyone with source access (CWE-798).

cwe: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials

extra.message: The response explicitly sets X-XSS-Protection to "0" and empties the Content-Security-Policy header, disabling browser-side protections against cross-site scripting and content injection for the endpoint's consumers (CWE-693/CWE-16).

cwe: CWE-693: Protection Mechanism Failure
CWE-16: Configuration

extra.message: The user-supplied fragment parameter is concatenated into a Jinja2 template string (Template("Result: " + fragment)) which is then rendered and returned as HTML. This is a server-side template injection allowing arbitrary expression evaluation and code execution, plus reflected XSS via HTMLResponse (CWE-94/CWE-79).

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

extra.message: The name query parameter is used directly in BASE_EXPORT_DIR / name to construct the destination path with no sanitization. A value containing path traversal sequences (e.g. ../../etc/x) escapes the target directory, allowing arbitrary file write of attacker-controlled bytes (CWE-22).

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: The host query parameter is concatenated into a shell command string passed to os.system("ping -c 1 " + host). A caller can inject shell metacharacters (e.g. ; rm -rf /) to execute arbitrary OS commands, leading to remote code execution (CWE-78).

cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')

extra.message: The nonce/code generator uses the non-cryptographic random module (random.choice) to produce what the endpoint names a nonce. random is predictable; security-relevant tokens must use secrets or a CSPRNG (CWE-338).

cwe: CWE-338: Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Number Generator (PRNG)

extra.message: The XML parser is created with load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, and no_network=False, and then used to parse the request body. External entity references are resolved, allowing an attacker to read local files, perform SSRF, or cause denial of service via crafted XML (CWE-611).

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: The endpoint returns os.environ.get("APP_ENV") and the stringified BASE_EXPORT_DIR server path in the JSON response, exposing internal environment configuration and filesystem layout to callers (CWE-200).

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: The user-supplied JSON (payload.get("filter", payload)) is passed directly to MongoDB find_one(query). A caller can submit operator injection (e.g. {"$where": "..."} or {"$ne": null}) to bypass query logic or exfiltrate records (CWE-943).

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic

extra.message: The session authentication cookie is set with secure=False. Because the cookie carries the user's session token, it can be transmitted over plaintext HTTP and intercepted by a network attacker (CWE-614).

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute

extra.message: The default database_url embeds hard-coded credentials (postgres:postgres) in source. Anyone with code access learns the database password, and it cannot be rotated without a code/env change (CWE-798).

cwe: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials

extra.message: When importing tenants via CSV, if no password is supplied the account is created with the hard-coded default password "TenantPass123!" (hash_password(row.get("password", "TenantPass123!"))). All imported tenants without an explicit password share a publicly known credential, enabling account takeover (CWE-259).

cwe: CWE-259: Use of Hard-coded Password
CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials

extra.message: DEMO_PASSWORD = "Password123!" is a hard-coded credential used to seed every demo account. The same known password is shared across all seeded users, so anyone aware of the seed value can authenticate as any demo account (CWE-798).

cwe: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
